title: Three Rounds and One Short Wrap
subtitle: 竞技健身 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 竞技健身（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·竞技与健身）
meta: 主题语境：竞技健身（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·竞技与健身）　|　核心词汇：fist　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 fist 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1964 the trainer ① clenched a fist that no referee in the ring would have counted, and he said the clenching was the whole of the round. The ② fist, meaning the hand itself and not the palm, ran three rounds and stayed uncounted in the book; a fist, he said, is the only thing in a ring that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ fist in that ring had the same short wrap beside it, and the ④ fist at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A fist, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the trainer said the counting is the part that fills three rounds.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the fist was the whole of the matter, meaning the grip and not the hand. The ⑥ fist, meaning the grip and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; fist, he said, is either something you clench or the only word that means both a hand and a grip. He said the grip is the part they remember.

By 1971 the ⑦ fist had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short wrap. The ⑧ fist of the whole thing, the trainer wrote in May, was one ring and three rounds of counting; fist, he said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ fist I remember is the one counted in the plan, which closed in 1973 and is still described as the quietest in the ring. A ⑩ fist, my mother said in 1975, is the only one that improves by being counted; every fist, she said, is a grip that has agreed to look like a hand. She said the grip was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 拳；拳头（指拳台上每一只旁边的那一只）
B. n. 拳（指那一只本身，与手掌相对）
C. 固定搭配：clench a fist 握紧一只拳头
D. n. 拳（指留给孩子们的那一只）
E. n. 拳（抽象总称，指一座拳台的握拳之事）
F. n. 拳（指计划里写到、被数过的那一只）
G. n. 铁腕；掌控（the iron fist，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）
H. n. 铁腕（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西）

items.q: clenched a fist that no referee in the ring would have counted
The fist, meaning the hand itself and not the palm
the fist at the far side
the fist was the whole of the matter
the fist had become a line in a plan
The fist of the whole thing
A fist, my mother said in 1975

answers.why: clench a fist 意为“握紧一只拳头”，1964 年那位教练握紧了一只拳台上没有一位裁判肯数过的拳头。
fist 意为“拳”，指那一只本身而不是手掌，它经过了三个回合而在簿子上没有被数过。
fist 意为“拳”，指拳台上每一只旁边的那一只，每一只旁边都有同一条短短的绑带。
fist 意为“拳”，指留给孩子们的那一只，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
fist 意为“铁腕、掌控”，指一件事里人人都等却无人说破的那样东西，叔叔说这份铁腕就是那件事的全部。
fist 意为“铁腕”，指人人都等却无人说破的那样东西而不是那只拳头，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
fist 意为“拳”，指计划里写到、被数过的那一只，到 1971 年这一只成了计划里的一行。
fist 意为“拳”，教练五月写道，整件事的握拳之事是一座拳台和三个回合的数过。
fist 意为“拳”，我记得的是计划里数过的那一只，1973 年结束了，至今仍被说成拳台上最安静的一只。
fist 为抽象总称，母亲 1975 年说，一只拳头是唯一会因为被好好数过而变得更好的东西。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1964 年那位教练握紧了一只拳台上没有一位裁判肯数过的拳头，他说握拳才是那个回合的全部。（clench a fist）
那只拳头，指的是那一只本身而不是手掌，经过了三个回合而在簿子上没有被数过。（fist）
那座拳台上每一只拳头旁边都有同一条短短的绑带。（fist）
最远那一侧那只拳头，指的是他们留给孩子们的那一只，是唯一有人谢过两次的。（fist）
叔叔说这份铁腕就是那件事的全部，指的是那样东西而不是那只拳头。（fist）
1975 年母亲说，一只拳头是唯一会因为被好好数过而变得更好的东西。（fist）
answers: In 1964 the trainer clenched a fist that no referee in the ring would have counted, and he said the clenching was the whole of the round.
The fist, meaning the hand itself and not the palm, ran three rounds and stayed uncounted in the book.
Every fist in that ring had the same short wrap beside it.
The fist at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice.
My uncle said the fist was the whole of the matter, meaning the grip and not the hand.
A fist, my mother said in 1975, is the only one that improves by being counted.
